lesson.title: Learning PINNs in PyTorch: 1D Diffusion Equation
lesson.goal: train a physics-informed neural network in PyTorch

sources.title: Learning PINNs in PyTorch: 1D Diffusion Equation

steps.title: Install pyDOE and import libraries
steps.instructions: Install pyDOE and import PyTorch, Matplotlib, NumPy, and lhs. Configure float32 default dtype, set random seeds to 1234, and select the CUDA or CPU device.

targets.caption: Import lhs for Latin Hypercube Sampling and configure PyTorch device and seeds

explanations.topic: Using pyDOE for Latin Hypercube Sampling of collocation points

hints: Which package provides Latin Hypercube Sampling for collocation points?
Use !pip install pyDOE and import lhs from pyDOE alongside torch and numpy.
Call torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float), set both torch and numpy seeds to 1234, and define device.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to install pyDOE before importing lhs.
Leaving PyTorch's default dtype mismatched or forgetting to set random seeds for reproducibility.

steps.title: Generate and plot exact solution
steps.instructions: Define f_real(x, t) for the exact diffusion solution and create a 200x100 meshgrid over x in [-1, 1] and t in [0, 1]. Evaluate y_real on the grid and visualize it with plot3D.

checks.label: Meshgrid created from x and t

targets.caption: Define the analytical solution and generate the 2D space-time grid

explanations.topic: Creating a 2D surface with torch.meshgrid over the problem domain

hints: How do you build a 2D grid from 1D linspace vectors in PyTorch?
Define f_real(x,t) returning torch.exp(-t)*(torch.sin(np.pi*x)) and call torch.meshgrid(x,t).
Use torch.linspace(-1,1,200) for x, torch.linspace(0,1,100) for t, evaluate f_real(X,T), and call plot3D(x,t,y_real).
common_mistakes: Using numpy functions instead of torch.exp and torch.sin on tensor inputs.
Swapping the domain intervals [-1, 1] for x and [0, 1] for t.

steps.title: Flatten meshgrid into testing data
steps.instructions: Transpose and flatten X, T, and y_real into column vectors using hstack and None indexing to build X_test and y_test. Store the lower and upper domain bounds in lb and ub and print the shapes.

targets.caption: Flatten the 200x100 grid into (20000, 2) test coordinates and extract bounds

explanations.topic: Column-major flattening of meshgrid matrices for a fully connected network

hints: Why does a fully connected network need flattened vectors instead of 200x100 matrices?
Transpose each matrix with .transpose(1,0), flatten it, and add a column axis with [:,None].
Stack X and T with torch.hstack into X_test, flatten y_real into y_test, and set lb=X_test[0], ub=X_test[-1].
common_mistakes: Omitting [:,None], which leaves tensors as 1D vectors instead of (20000, 1) columns.
Forgetting .transpose(1,0) before .flatten() when doing column-major flattening.

steps.title: Sample initial and boundary points
steps.instructions: Extract the initial condition (left_X, left_Y) and both spatial boundaries (bottom_X/Y, top_X/Y) and stack them into X_train and Y_train. Randomly sample Nu=100 points without replacement into X_train_Nu and Y_train_Nu.

targets.caption: Combine IC and BC points and randomly sample Nu=100 training points

explanations.topic: Mapping initial and boundary conditions to edges of the domain grid

hints: Which rows or columns of X and T correspond to t=0, x=-1, and x=1?
Slice [:,0] for t=0, [0,:] for x=-1, and [-1,:] for x=1, then vertically stack them with torch.vstack.
Sample Nu=100 indices using np.random.choice(X_train.shape[0], Nu, replace=False) and index X_train and Y_train.
common_mistakes: Calling .unsqueeze(1) or [:,None] inconsistently, causing a dimension mismatch in torch.vstack.
Sampling with replace=True or using torch.hstack instead of torch.vstack when combining boundaries.

steps.title: Sample collocation points and move tensors
steps.instructions: Generate Nf=10000 collocation points inside [lb, ub] with lhs(2, Nf) and stack them with X_train_Nu. Cast the training/testing tensors to float, create the zero tensor f_hat, and move everything to device.

targets.caption: Sample 10000 collocation points and move all tensors to device

explanations.topic: Scaling Latin Hypercube samples to the domain and creating f_hat zeros

hints: How do you scale unit-cube samples from lhs(2, Nf) to your [lb, ub] domain?
Compute lb + (ub - lb) * lhs(2, Nf) and stack X_train_Nu onto X_train_Nf with torch.vstack.
Create f_hat = torch.zeros(X_train_Nf.shape[0], 1).to(device) and move X_train_Nu, Y_train_Nu, X_train_Nf, X_test, and y_test to device.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to convert X_train_Nf (which becomes float64 from numpy lhs) with .float() before passing it to the model.
Forgetting to move f_hat or X_test/y_test to the same device as the model.

steps.title: Implement the FCN PINN class
steps.instructions: Define class FCN(nn.Module) with Tanh activations, Xavier weight initialization, and a forward pass over layers. Implement lossBC, lossPDE using autograd.grad for u_t and u_xx, and total loss.

targets.caption: Compute PDE derivatives via autograd.grad and combine BC and PDE losses

explanations.topic: Architecture, Xavier initialization, and forward pass of FCN
Computing u_t and u_xx with autograd.grad in lossPDE

hints: How do you differentiate the network output with respect to its inputs x and t?
Clone x_PDE with requires_grad=True, run self.forward(g), and call autograd.grad twice with create_graph=True.
Extract f_t = f_x_t[:,[1]] and f_xx = f_xx_tt[:,[0]], assemble the residual f, and return self.loss_function(f, f_hat).
common_mistakes: Omitting retain_graph=True or create_graph=True on the first autograd.grad call, which breaks second-order differentiation.
Applying self.activation to the final linear layer in forward().

steps.title: Instantiate PINN and run training
steps.instructions: Instantiate FCN with layers [2, 32, 64, 1], move it to device, and create an Adam optimizer with lr=1e-3. Train for 20000 iterations and print training and testing losses every 2000 steps.

targets.caption: Set up Adam optimizer and run the 20000-iteration training loop

explanations.topic: Choosing input/output layer sizes and configuring Adam optimizer
Evaluating test loss inside torch.no_grad() during training

hints: What must the first and last entries of the layers array be?
Set layers=np.array([2,32,64,1]), instantiate PINN=FCN(layers).to(device), and configure Adam with lr=1e-3.
In the loop, call optimizer.zero_grad(), loss.backward(), and optimizer.step(), logging test_loss inside with torch.no_grad().
common_mistakes: Passing a negative learning rate like lr=1e-3 typoed as -3.
Forgetting optimizer.zero_grad() before loss.backward(), which accumulates gradients across steps.

steps.title: Evaluate model and plot predictions
steps.instructions: Compute predictions y1 = PINN(X_test) and reshape x1, t1, y1, and y_test back into 100x200 transposed matrices on CPU. Call plot3D_Matrix to compare the PINN solution against the exact solution.

targets.caption: Evaluate the trained PINN on X_test, reshape outputs, and plot

explanations.topic: Reshaping flattened prediction vectors back to 2D matrices for plotting

hints: How do you convert the 20000-element GPU tensor y1 back into a plottable 2D grid?
Reshape each vector to [100,200], transpose(1,0), and call .detach().cpu().
Run plot3D_Matrix(arr_x1, arr_T1, arr_y1) and compare with plot3D_Matrix(X, T, y_real).
common_mistakes: Forgetting .detach().cpu() before plotting a GPU tensor with gradients attached.
Reshaping to [200,100] instead of [100,200] before transposing.
